title: Indexing a term preserves the count of matching literals
statement: Let $t$ be a term over $n$ variables, that is, a finite list of literals, and let $p$ be a predicate on literals. Form from $t$ the indexed list in which each literal is paired with its position in $t$. Then the number of entries of this indexed list whose literal component satisfies $p$ equals the number of literals of $t$ that satisfy $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $t$ is a term (finite list of literals) over $n$ variables
$p$ is a Boolean predicate on literals
replaced:
Filtering $t.\mathrm{zipIdx}$ by a predicate on the literal component has the same
length as filtering the original term $t$ by the same predicate.
